title: Normalized opposite-root Gauss chart in relative semisimple rank one
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $H/S$ a reductive group (smooth affine of finite presentation, with connected reductive geometric fibres) in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Let $M$ be a finite-rank free abelian group, $T=D_A(M)\hookrightarrow H$ a closed subgroup [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group, def-weil-closed-immersion] whose geometric fibres are maximal tori, and $a\in M\setminus\{0\}$. For every $m\in M$, let $\chi_m:T\to\mathbf G_{m,A}$ be the monomial character. Put $\mathfrak h=\ker(H(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to H(A))$, with its tangent $A$-module structure and the full conjugation coaction $\rho:\mathfrak h\to\mathfrak h\otimes_A A[M]$, and put $P_m=\{v:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$. Suppose every geometric fibre has exactly the nonzero torus weights $\{a,-a\}$, both $P_a$ and $P_{-a}$ are free of rank one, and the natural inclusions give $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(T)\oplus P_a\oplus P_{-a}$. Fix a generator $X\in P_a$.

Write $\mathbf G_a(B)=(B,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(B)=B^\times$ for every commutative $A$-algebra $B$. There is a unique triple $(x_+,x_-,h)$ of $S$-group homomorphisms $x_\pm:\mathbf G_a\to H$ and $h:\mathbf G_m\to T$ with the following properties. The maps $x_\pm$ are closed immersions, $T$-equivariant for the actions $t\cdot u=\chi_{\pm a}(t)u$, and their tangent vectors $dx_+(1)=X$, $dx_-(1)\in P_{-a}$ are generators. Multiplication
$$\mathbf G_a\times_S T\times_S\mathbf G_a\longrightarrow H,\qquad(v,t,u)\longmapsto x_-(v)t x_+(u)$$
is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], with image $\Omega$. For every $A$-algebra $B$ and $u,v\in B$, the point $x_+(u)x_-(v)$ lies in $\Omega(B)$ if and only if $w=1+uv\in B^\times$, and whenever this holds,
$$x_+(u)x_-(v)=x_-(v/w)h(w)x_+(u/w).$$
All assertions concern the full group schemes and all test algebras, including nonreduced ones. There is no Noetherian, connectedness or residue-characteristic assumption on $A$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem 4.1.4 and its proof, printed pp.110,116-118; Theorem 4.2.6, printed pp.120-121, normalized by a generator of the positive root line. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this rank-one structural theorem.

proof.text: Choose any generator $Y_0$ of $P_{-a}$. Apply [lem-sfb-reductive-framed-noetherian-descent] to $G=H$, $\Psi=\{a,-a\}$, $X_a=X$, $X_{-a}=Y_0$. It gives a nonzero finitely generated integer subring $A_0\subseteq A$, a reductive pair $(H_0,T_0=D_{A_0}(M))$, and generators $X_0,Y_{0,0}$ with the same full coaction decomposition. Every geometric fibre of $H_0$ has semisimple rank one and roots $\{a,-a\}$. Thus the Noetherian hypothesis needed by the existing relative structural lemmas is satisfied over $A_0$, without imposing it on $A$.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11, printed pp.88-89, with the framed tangent data; agent reduction to the existing Noetherian structural statements.

proof.text: Choose a lattice basis $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential] over $A_0$ to both root lines and pull back to $A$. Its arbitrary-base-change clause supplies closed maps $e_\pm:V(P_{\pm a})\to H$, uniquely determined by tangent inclusion and $T$-equivariance even after any further algebra extension. Define $x_+(u)=e_+(uX)$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model] to $(H_0,T_0,a)$. All its hypotheses hold by step 1: smoothness, affine finite type, reductive fibres, maximal torus and semisimple rank one. Pull its affine open cover and its inverse isomorphisms back to $S$. We obtain affine opens $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ covering $S$, on each of which $(H,T)$ is a central split torus times one of the three indicated matrix pairs, with $a$ the ratio of diagonal entries. These chosen models remain valid over every $R_i$-algebra.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4, printed pp.110,116-118; Theorem 5.1.8 and Corollary 5.1.9 proof, pp.139-141, matrix realization of the rank-one calculation.

proof.text: Work on one such open, and suppress the identity in the central torus. Put $U(z)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&z\\ 0&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $L(z)=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&0\\ z&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, taking their classes in the projective case. The positive tangent generator is $X=cE_{12}$ for a unit $c\in R_i^\times$. The standard maps $U$ and $L$ are group homomorphisms, closed immersions and equivariant for the ratio character and its inverse. By uniqueness of the canonical exponentials, including after base change, $x_+(u)=U(cu)$ and $e_-(v c^{-1}E_{21})=L(c^{-1}v)$. Define local candidates $x_{-,i}(v)=L(c^{-1}v)$ and $h_i(w)=\operatorname{diag}(w,w^{-1})$, with trivial central-torus component. Their tangent vectors are generators and they are group homomorphisms. The closed-image assertions follow from the closed canonical exponential and a change of basis of its line; in the projective case the off-diagonal tangent coordinates are also $E_{12},E_{21}$, including in characteristic two.

source.place: Example 4.2.1, printed pp.115-116; linked coordinates after Theorem 4.2.6, p.121; Corollary 5.1.9 proof, p.141.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-relative-block-gauss-chart] with two blocks of size one. For $g=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}p&q\\ r&s\end{smallmatrix}\right)\in\operatorname{GL}_2(B)$ with $p$ a unit, its unique factors are
$$g=L(r/p)\operatorname{diag}(p,\det(g)/p)U(q/p).$$
Restricting $\det(g)=1$ gives the $\operatorname{SL}_2$ chart. For the projective quotient, the condition that $p$ be a unit is invariant under multiplying a lift by a scalar unit, hence defines the open quotient chart. A lift on this chart has the unique scalar-normalized representative $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&b\\ d&e\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, where $e-bd$ is a unit. Local normalized lifts agree, so this description holds also for projective points lacking a global matrix lift. The inverse chart coordinates are $L(d)$, $[\operatorname{diag}(1,e-bd)]$ and $U(b)$. Consequently lower times diagonal times upper is an open immersion in each of the three models. Multiplying the unipotent parameters by $c^{-1},c$ and retaining the central torus gives the required local multiplication chart. Its factors are unique over every algebra.

source.place: Example 4.2.5, printed pp.119-120; explicit projective quotient chart; arbitrary-ring Gauss chart specializes to two one-dimensional blocks.

proof.text:
Direct multiplication gives
$$U(cu)L(c^{-1}v)=\begin{pmatrix}1+uv&cu\\ c^{-1}v&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
By step 4 this lies in the lower-diagonal-upper chart exactly when $w=1+uv$ is a unit. If so its three factors are $L(c^{-1}v/w)$, $\operatorname{diag}(w,w^{-1})$ and $U(cu/w)$. Passing to projective classes gives the same identity and the same unit criterion: the top-left entry of this explicit lift is $w$. Central components are identities. These equalities are regular formulas in $R_i[u,v,(1+uv)^{-1}]$, so hold on every test algebra, with no unit assumption on $u$ or $v$. This proves all required assertions for the local candidates.

source.place: Example 4.2.5 and equation (4.2.1), printed pp.119-121; the displayed two-by-two matrix multiplication.

proof.text:
We prove local uniqueness over every $R_i$-algebra $R$. In any candidate triple the positive map is $U(cu)$ by the uniqueness assertion of [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential]. Its negative tangent generator is $dE_{21}$ for a unit $d\in R^\times$; the same assertion makes its negative map $L(dv)$. Its chart is therefore the same open as in step 4. Take $u=1,v=\epsilon$ in $R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. Comparing the unique upper coordinates in its asserted Gauss formula gives
$$c/(1+cd\epsilon)=c/(1+\epsilon).$$
Since $c$ is a unit, comparison of the $\epsilon$ coefficients gives $cd=1$, valid even if $R$ is nonreduced or has characteristic two. Thus the negative map is forced to be $L(c^{-1}v)$. Finally take $u=1,v=t-1$ over $R[t,t^{-1}]$. The now fixed unipotent factors and uniqueness of the whole torus factor in step 4 force $h(t)=\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$ with identity central component. This is equality of morphisms by the universal invertible coordinate $t$, not equality only on field-valued points. Hence the local triple is unique after arbitrary base change.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.6 uniqueness, printed pp.121-125; agent coefficient argument using dual numbers and the universal unit, retaining nilpotent information.

proof.text: On overlaps of the opens $S_i$, step 6 identifies the two local triples; its proof applies to any further algebra, so equality can be checked on affine opens of each overlap. The covering is fpqc by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale], and its pullbacks to $\mathbf G_a$, $\mathbf G_m$ and all products are fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to glue the local $x_{-,i}$ and $h_i$ uniquely. Their group and equivariance identities hold globally by the equality part of this same descent statement on the product covers. The local negative tangent generators glue to a global basis $Y$ of $P_{-a}$: relative to the fixed basis $Y_0$, their scalar coefficients and their reciprocals agree and glue as sections of the structure sheaf. Thus $x_-(v)=e_-(vY)$ by the canonical uniqueness already established in step 2. In particular $x_-$ is a closed immersion, as is $x_+$, and $dx_-(1)=Y$.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 and Theorem 4.2.6, uniqueness and gluing; Stacks Tags 022C, 022D(3), 023Q.

proof.text: Let $\Omega_i$ be the local open images in step 4. Their restrictions agree on overlaps since the multiplication morphisms agree. Their union is an open $\Omega\subseteq H$. The local inverse maps from $\Omega_i$ to $\mathbf G_a\times T\times\mathbf G_a$ agree, since each is inverse to that same multiplication map. Glue them by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], using [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-finer-than-etale] and [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] for the covers; this is a global inverse and proves the open immersion. For any $A$-algebra $B$, its spectrum is covered by the pulls of the $S_i$. Step 5 says that the product factors through $\Omega$ on this cover exactly when $1+uv$ is locally a unit. Local inverses of a fixed element agree, so this is equivalent to being a unit in $B$. The identity of step 5 then holds globally by uniqueness of morphism descent. Any competing global triple restricts to our triple by step 6 and hence equals it by the same equality detection. If $B=0$ all schemes over its spectrum are empty and the formulas hold uniquely. Nothing used division by an integer, reducedness, or connectedness of $A$.
